content:
Grouping by ordering info and footnotes 1)/2): one mode per model, with transmit wavelength ranges and centers tied to each part number. Shared 50GbE / IEEE 802.3cd and 52.125 Gbps line rate apply to both.

```json
{
  "modes": [
    {
      "label": "2930 Tx 1294.40nm / Rx 1308.24nm BiDi 50GbE",
      "model": "SO-QSFP28-50GE-BX40D-2930",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1292.21,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1296.59,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1294.4,
      "standards_code": "IEEE802.3cd",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 52.125
    },
    {
      "label": "3029 Tx 1308.24nm / Rx 1294.40nm BiDi 50GbE",
      "model": "SO-QSFP28-50GE-BX40D-3029",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1306.29,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1310.19,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1308.24,
      "standards_code": "IEEE802.3cd",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 52.125
    }
  ]
}
```

**Evidence:** Footnote 1) maps 2930 to transmit 1292.21–1296.59 nm (center 1294.40 nm); footnote 2) maps 3029 to 1306.29–1310.19 nm (center 1308.24 nm). The technical table lists **50GbE IEEE802.3cd** and **52.125 Gbps** once for the pair; footnote 4’s **53.125 Gbps** is the host/FEC rate for the same 50GbE receiver test, not a separate operating mode. **50GbE** as a second `standards_code` atom is the service name alongside IEEE 802.3cd, not model-specific—only **IEEE802.3cd** is used per field. **50.0** Gbps is not stated as a separate line rate in the excerpt. No mode-specific penalties appear in the supplied atoms.
